audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 matches 53.76% over 1090 games: Xerath has no dash and no self-peel, only Shocking Orb (E) at 13s, so every stage of lane belongs to Irelia and only his artillery range threatens her outside it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike called Rite of the Arcane a 'global-range execute'. It is a self-immobilizing channel of barrages, not an execute.
audit.why: Wrong ability description on the enemy's biggest spike.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike rewritten: the channel roots him in place and Flawless Duet cancels it. First item spike aligned to Blade of the Ruined King (report[8] already names the on-hit build).
sources: enemyKit R text and channel flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Shocking Orb was called a 'root' in whys[3], spikes[2], mid and late. It is a stun. The applicable interaction that Flawless Duet (E) cancels his Rite of the Arcane channel was absent everywhere.
audit.why: A stun and a root behave differently for a player deciding whether to dash, and the R-cancel is the single highest-value interaction in the matchup.
audit.corrected: All four 'root' references corrected to stun; the R-cancel written into whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d claimed a 'fifteen-second invitation' with no source.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and only 11s at rank 5 — the invented 15s was both unsourced and wrong.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written: Shocking Orb 13s to 11s, Arcanopulse 9s at 80 mana, Rite of the Arcane 130s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Bodies did not match their titles.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Check it before every step-up. - W Defiant Dance is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb (E) is his only CC and barely scales down: 13s at rank 1, still 11s at rank 5 — dodge it and his artillery never converts. - Arcanopulse (Q) is 9s at rank 1 and costs 80 mana, so early poke drains him fast. - Rite of the Arcane (R) is 130s at rank 1.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Bladesurge (Q) and Flawless Duet (E) each stack the passive; arrive at four before you touch him, or bonus on-hit damage never funds the kill.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a Bladesurge charge; shove the wave away and you must walk 1050 units under his poke.

edits.before: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — that is 13 seconds of open ground.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb from 1050 range, poking you off the wave, and shelling you from outside your reach.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by hunting the immobile one: he has no dash, and Vanguard's Edge walls the only exit he was counting on.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Xerath's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, take his vision away: he needs 1050-range sightlines, so fight in his half where minions and walls break them.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 hold as his root is his only real answer and it's often on cooldown
edits.after: Levels 4-5 hold: Shocking Orb stuns, is his only answer, and is 13s down

edits.before: Ultimate execute needs setup time your dash denies, favour stays with you at level 6
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane is a channel — your Flawless Duet stun cancels it outright

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane is a global-range execute, but at close range it's slow to land, so dash in and burst him before he can land the full combo.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane immobilizes him for the whole channel and Flawless Duet cancels it — hold your stun for the cast, not for his step-back.

edits.before: Trinity or Sunderer lets you kill him in one combo before his root-into-burst sequence finishes, so all-in as soon as items complete.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King kills him in one reset chain before his Shocking Orb stun and Arcanopulse sequence finishes, so all-in on it.

edits.before: From level 3 to 6 your gap-close continues to dominate: he needs a landed root to have any real answer, and even after his ultimate comes online you can dash in and burst him before the full combo lands.
edits.after: From level 3 to 6 your gap-close continues to dominate: he needs a landed Shocking Orb stun to have any answer, and once he channels Rite of the Arcane your Flawless Duet stun ends it on the spot.

edits.before: Your first item burst kills him fast before his root-into-combo finishes, and while a fully scaled Xerath can poke you down from max range late game, forcing all-ins and using minion cover keeps this matchup solidly in your favor.
edits.after: Your first item burst kills him before the Shocking Orb stun into Arcanopulse sequence finishes, and while a fully scaled Xerath shells you from 1050 range, forcing all-ins and using minion cover keeps this matchup solidly in your favor.

notes: Level chart is Irelia 7/7 and both layers agree, so no chart edits. Shocking Orb was described as a root in four places — it is a stun per Riot's text. dosFull[2].d carried an invented 'fifteen-second' cooldown; corrected to the kit's 13s.
